title: build: fix PyO3 linkage for cargo test; standalone supplementary.pdf
body:
## Summary

Fixes `cargo test` failing with PyO3 linker errors (`undefined symbol: PyErr_Restore`, `PyType_GetFlags`, …) while keeping `maturin develop --release` producing a proper extension module, and makes `supplementary.tex` compile to a standalone `supplementary.pdf`.

**Root cause:** `extension-module` was an unconditional `pyo3` feature. Cargo unifies features across normal and dev-dependencies, so it stayed active in test builds and suppressed linking to `libpython` — hence undefined `Py*` symbols at test link time.

**Fix:**
- `Cargo.toml`: `pyo3 = "0.22"` (no features); `extension-module` becomes an opt-in crate feature `extension-module = ["pyo3/extension-module"]`; `dev-dependencies.pyo3` gets `auto-initialize` so test binaries embed and initialize Python.
- `pyproject.toml` (new): declares the maturin backend and enables the `extension-module` feature only for wheel builds (`[tool.maturin] features = ["extension-module"]`).

**LaTeX:** `supplementary.tex` was a preamble-less fragment already inlined verbatim into `main.tex`. It now carries the same preamble as `main.tex` plus its own `\maketitle`, and the one cross-document `\eqref{eq:native-neutrino-normalization-check}` (a label defined only in `main.tex`) is replaced with a textual reference. Both `main.pdf` (87 pp) and `supplementary.pdf` (6 pp) compile clean under `latexmk`.

Also ignores LaTeX aux files and simulator output artifacts (`.h5`, `cosmo_*.csv`, `result_*.png`, …) in `.gitignore`.

## Validation

All gates pass on Ubuntu 22.04 / Python 3.10 / Rust 1.98:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release` | 19/19 pass |
| `precision_cosmology.py --run-tests` | 14/14 pass |
| `boltzmann_shbt.py --run-tests` | pass |
| `pytest tests/ -q` | 31/31 pass |
| `shbt_simulate.py` modes: audit, cosmology, baryogenesis, history, all, cosmology-test | all pass; `.json`/`.csv`/`.h5`/`.png` outputs generated |
| Custom runs: CLI params, `--config config.default.yaml`, programmatic `simulate({...})` API | pass; `eta_b = 6.449923359416131e-10` |
| `examples/run_audit.py` | pass; LaTeX macros generated |
| `latexmk main.tex`, `supplementary.tex` | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
